en: One fascicle of the Ritual Manual for the Heart Recitation of the Lotus Family of the Vajraśekhara [Sūtra].
Compiled by the Grand Master of State Ceremonial, Special Advancement, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
Duke of Sushan with a Fief of Three Thousand Households, conferred the purple robe and the posthumous title of Minister of Works, known as Dajian (Great Mirror).
I take refuge and pay homage to Samantabhadra, Who holds the vajra and lotus in his hands.
To explain the method for practicing yoga, One should first pay homage to the Triple Gem.
Kneeling with the long legs and joining the palms in the lotus gesture, One should direct the mind toward the assembly of noble ones.
One should confess transgressions and rejoice accordingly.
Next, contemplating all phenomena as being far removed from dust and defilement,
one should recite this mantra, whereby the vessel-world becomes entirely pure.
The Mantra for Purifying the Ground says:
Next, one should purify the three karmas; contemplating that all phenomena are fundamentally pure, by reciting this mantra-vidyā, the three karmas are all purified.
The mantra for purifying the body is as follows:
By means of this mantra, one's body becomes a vessel of the Dharma;
one contemplates the Buddhas within the void, filling it completely like sesame seeds.
Then, by reciting the Universal Illumination [Mantra], one clearly beholds all the Buddhas.
The Mantra for Contemplating the Buddha is as follows:
Visualize the syllable HŪṂ at the heart, which transforms into a five-pronged vajra.
One should imagine that throughout the entire body, there are as many Vajrasattvas as there are atoms;
with vajra-palms extended and arms outstretched,
one prostrates with the whole body cast upon the ground, relinquishing the body so it pervades the entire dharma-realm.
Offer this to the Honored One Akṣobhya, and perform all rites of service for the Buddhas.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, visualize the syllable TRAḤ at the vajra-jewel on the forehead.
Visualize your body as the form of a jewel; within the body, visualize the number of atoms as the Vajra-treasury.
Prostrate with the entire body, touching the forehead to the ground, and place the vajra-palms at the heart to offer to the Honored One Ratnasambhava.
Visualize yourself within infinite realms, wearing the crown of the five Buddhas upon your head and consecrating the crowns of all Buddhas.
The mantra is as follows:
Visualize the syllable Hrīḥ at the mouth, and immediately imagine an eight-petaled lotus;
visualize one's own body as a lotus flower, and within that body, as numerous as atoms, imagine the formation of the Vajradharma;
then prostrate with the entire body using the mouth.
Placing the vajra-palms at the crown of the head, one makes an offering to Amitāyus;
visualizing [him] pervading the assemblies of all Buddhas, one requests him to turn the wheel of Dharma.
The mantra says:
Visualize the syllable *Aḥ* at the crown of the head, which transforms into the Karma-vajra;
contemplate one’s entire body as the Universal Vajra. Within the body, all atoms become Karma-vajras;
with the whole body, perform prostration with the crown of the head.
With the vajra-palm held before the heart, offer this to the Honored One Amoghasiddhi;
visualizing the Universal Assembly, contemplate the body of Vajrakarma and perform the great offering.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the Great Seal of Vajradhara: interlace the fingers of the dhyāna- and prajñā-hands with the thumbs and little fingers crossed;
place the right knee on the ground and rest [the seal] upon the crown of the head, visualizing each instance as prostrating at the feet of the Tathāgata.
Extending the fingers from the crown like hanging ribbons, rotate them from the heart in a dancing motion,
and place the vajra-palms upon the crown.
The mantra is as follows:
I take refuge in the Perfectly Awakened Ones of the ten directions, the Supreme Dharma, and the assembly of Bodhisattvas;
with the pure karma of body, speech, and mind, I reverently prostrate with palms joined in earnest devotion.
Throughout the beginningless cycle of existence within the various realms of being, whatever sins have been produced by the actions of body,
speech, and mind— just as the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have confessed them, so do I now present my confession.
Within the practices and vows of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, I rejoice in all the merit produced by the three vajra-actions,
as well as all the roots of goodness accumulated by Pratyekabuddhas, Śrāvakas, and all sentient beings.
The Lamp of All Worlds sits upon the terrace of enlightenment; With the eye of awakening fully blossomed, he illuminates the three realms of existence.
I now kneel before you and first entreat you: Please turn the supreme and wondrous wheel of Dharma.
To all Tathāgatas, lords of the triple world, who are about to enter parinirvāṇa without remainder,
I entreat you all to remain for a long time, not forsaking your compassionate vows to save the world.
Through the merit of repentance, sympathetic joy, and entreaty, may I never lose the bodhicitta;
among the sublime assemblies of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, may I always have virtuous friends who never weary of me or abandon me;
may I be free from the eight difficulties and be born where there are no hardships; and may my body be adorned with the marks of wisdom dwelling in past lives.
Far removed from delusion, endowed with compassion and wisdom, They are able to fully perfect all the pāramitās;
Born into noble lineages of abundant wealth and prosperity, With vast retinues that are ever flourishing,
Possessing the four unhindered analytical knowledges and the ten masteries, And the six supernormal powers and all dhyānas— these are all perfected.
Just as Vajradhvaja and Samantabhadra did, may my praise and dedication be likewise.
Following the vast aspirations of the practitioner, one should next arouse the supreme mind,
wishing that all sentient beings may possess those qualities praised by the Tathāgatas.
In both the mundane and supramundane realms, one shall swiftly attain supreme siddhi.
The mantra is:
Maṭha represents the two eyes; one should visualize Aṅga as the sun and moon.
Forming the double vajra-fists, place each at the side of the waist;
gaze everywhere into the space before you. All the Buddhas are filled with joy;
all the incense, flowers, and other articles of offering—
Therefore, by beholding with the eyes, one removes defilements to achieve purity and expels obstacles to establish the boundary.
The mantra is as follows:
The two wings of merit and wisdom joined together, with the ten perfections first interlaced,
are called the Vajra Palm, the foremost of all mudrās.
The mantra is as follows:
Then, with those same vajra-palms, form ten fingers into fists;
this is called the Vajrabandha, which is able to untie the bonds of the fetters and latent tendencies.
The mantra is as follows:
By means of the vajra-bond, one can purify the eighth consciousness and eliminate the seeds of defilement;
visualizing the two syllables *traṭ* placed upon both breasts, one forms the vajra-bond with both hands.
To open it like a door-panel,
the mantra is as follows:
With the vajra-bond, bend the wisdom-finger (middle finger) into the palm.
Generosity, wisdom, and precepts first open the way; through visualization, one summons the outflow-free wisdom and enters into the ālayavijñāna.
The mantra is as follows:
Then, with the same previous mudrā, extend the forceful fingers to support the wisdom fingers and place them against the gate of the heart;
thus, untainted wisdom becomes firm and stable.
The mantra is as follows:
Forming the two-fold vajra-bind, with the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhi* fingers extended upright like needles;
as soon as the mantra has been recited, one’s own body becomes Samantabhadra,
seated upon a lunar disc, while visualizing Samantabhadra before oneself.
The mantra says:
The practitioner should next form the Great Vow of Reality mudrā:
with both hands in the vajra-bind, extend the thumbs and the ring fingers.
Interlace the fingers of the hands of patience and aspiration, joining the surfaces of the fingertips;
piercing the heart with two fingers is called the "Arrow of Great Compassion," used to shoot at the mind of weary detachment,
[thereby attaining] the Samaya of Supreme Joy.
Be mindful of your original vow.
The mantra says:
Next, the practitioner should bind the Great Seal of Trailokyavijaya.
With two wrathful fists, the thumbs and wisdom fingers hook back-to-back,
while the index and middle fingers of both hands stand upright behind them.
Having eight arms and four faces, his form is smiling, wrathful, and terrifying.
With four blazing fangs and a body ablaze, the right foot extended and the left drawn back,
he tramples upon Mahādeva and his consort.
Rotating throughout the ten directions, turning to the left, he performs the rite of expulsion.
Turning to the right, one forms the boundary.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the Vajra-lotus; with both hands, form the Vajra-bind.
Generosity, wisdom, meditation, and knowledge stand upright;
through the lotus samaya, one attains the Lotus Family and becomes a sovereign wheel-turner.
The mantra is as follows:
Within the ālayavijñāna, which opposes the seeds of bodhi,
next one binds the Dharma-wheel mudrā to destroy that wheel of aversion and renunciation;
this is the aforementioned lotus mudrā, with the thumbs and wisdom-fingers interlaced and held upright.
Tearing and wrenching at one's own mind, one immediately extinguishes the seeds of the two vehicles.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the Great Desire Seal; with both hands in the Vajra-bond, [proceed].
Entering the wisdom-tiger’s mouth, one enters and exits with each recitation.
The mantra is:
*Oṃ surata-vajra jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ samaya-stvam*. This is the body of Great Bliss Amoghasiddhi; the mudrā is the same as above.
May all sentient beings universally Swiftly realize the stage of the Tathāgata;
Practitioners of yoga Should give rise to such a mind.
Having brought sentient beings to fulfillment, One should next summon all.
Spontaneously accomplishing great profound wisdom, fulfilling the great aspiration for bodhi,
and perfecting the seed of great compassion.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the mudrā for summoning sins:
with both hands in the vajra-bond, extend the ring and little fingers like needles, and bend the index and middle fingers like hooks.
Arousing a heart of great compassion, visualize [the deity] coming and going.
Summoning the sins of all sentient beings, the three evil destinies are drawn into one's own body;
all transgressions are summoned into the palm, appearing black like clouds and mist,
in the forms of many various spirits.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, form the mudrā for destroying transgressions: interlace the eight fingers with palms facing inward, and extend the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhi* fingers upright as before.
One should transform one's own body into Trailokyavijaya;
chanting the mantra with a resolute voice, one should give rise to compassion within the mind.
With the mudrās of patience and aspiration, one should perform three rhythmic beats to destroy the sins of all sentient beings.
The three evils are all dispelled.
The mantra says:
Next, purify the obstacles of the three karmas, causing determinate karma to be extinguished.
With the two vajra-palms, bend the second joints of the thumbs and forefingers, and press the ring fingers against the middle fingers;
by forming this mudrā, karmic obstacles are eliminated.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, one accomplishes the bodhicitta, bringing both self and others to fulfillment.
Forming the mudrā like a lotus, place it on the left side of the crown.
The mantra is as follows:
Directing the mind toward all sentient beings through the majesty of the Tathāgata Candrottara,
one will swiftly become like Samantabhadra, as described in the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra*.
One should sit in the full lotus posture, with limbs and joints unmoving;
one should form the seal of meditative concentration (*samādhi-mudrā*), binding the two hands in the vajra-bind and placing them facing upward beneath the navel;
keeping the body upright, one must not waver.
With the tongue pressed against the upper palate, bring the breath to rest and make it subtle;
contemplate the nature of all phenomena as arising entirely from one's own mind—
afflictions and secondary afflictions, the aggregates, elements, and sense bases.
All are like illusions and mirages, like the city of the gandharvas, and like a whirling firebrand; they are also like echoes in an empty valley.
Having contemplated thus with discernment, one perceives neither body nor mind.
Abiding in the equality of quiescent extinction, one realizes the ultimate wisdom of reality.
Then, within the midst of emptiness, one beholds all Buddhas as numerous as sesame seeds,
filling the entire realm of space.
He conceived that he had personally realized the ten stages and dwelt within the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*).
Then, all the Tathāgatas in the sky snapped their fingers to awaken him, saying:
"Good son, the state you have realized is but a single path of purity."
Even the diamond-like samādhi and the wisdom of omniscience (sarvajñajñāna) have not yet been realized through this alone.
Do not take this to be final; one must fulfill the vows of Samantabhadra before attaining supreme perfect enlightenment.
With body and mind unmoving, one pays homage to all Buddhas within meditative concentration.
The mantra is as follows:
Upon hearing the awakening call, the practitioner, having universally paid homage within concentration, [recites:]...
“I only pray that all Tathāgatas will show me the sphere of my practice.
The Buddhas spoke with one voice:
“You should contemplate your own mind.”
Having heard this teaching, he contemplated his own mind as instructed;
dwelling long in earnest observation, he did not perceive any characteristic of his own mind.
He then again imagined prostrating at the Buddha’s feet and addressed the Most Victorious Honored One:
"I do not see my own mind; what are the characteristics of this mind?
All the Buddhas replied:
"The characteristics of the mind are difficult to fathom."
Bestow the heart-mantra and immediately recite the penetrating heart-vidyā;
visualize the mind as a lunar disc, observing it with correct reasoning as if within a light mist.
The mantra says:
The storehouse consciousness is fundamentally not defiled; it is pure and free from blemish.
Because it possesses merit and wisdom, one’s own mind is like the full moon.
He further reflects in this way:
"What is this mind? It is the seed of the habitual tendencies of afflictions; both good and evil arise entirely from the mind."
The mind is the ālaya; by cultivating purity as its cause, and through the perfuming of the six perfections, that mind becomes the Great Mind.
The storehouse consciousness is fundamentally not defiled; it is pure and free from all blemish.
Having accumulated merit and wisdom over a long period, it is likened to the pure, full moon.
Being without essence and without objective reality, it cannot even be called a "moon";
yet because it is endowed with merit and wisdom, one's own mind is like the full moon.
Leaping with a heart full of joy, he again addressed all the World-Honored Ones:
"Having perceived my own mind, it is pure like the full moon,
free from the stains of all afflictions, as well as from the grasper and the grasped."
All the Buddhas spoke thus:
"Obscured by adventitious defilements, the bodhicitta is impure;
contemplate the pure lunar disc, and you shall realize the bodhicitta."
Bestow this heart-mantra, reciting it secretly while observing: The mantra is:
Oṃ jñānadhātu-mudrā-pūjaye. It causes the moon-disc of the mind to become perfectly full and increasingly radiant.
The Buddhas spoke again:
"The bodhicitta is firm.
They then bestowed the heart-mantra:
"Oṃ sūkṣma-vajra. The mantra for visualizing the five-pronged vajra lotus is as follows:
"Visualize an eight-petaled lotus within a pure moon disc, pervading the entire dharmadhātu;
let it become a single, great lotus."
One should know that one’s own body is the vajra-lotus realm.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vajratmakūhana. One’s own body becomes a lotus, pure and free from attachment.
Again, he addressed the Buddhas, saying:
"I am the Lotus-Body.
Then those Tathāgatas commanded the practitioner, saying:
"Contemplate the body as the deity.
Then, he bestowed this mantra:
"Having already become the body of the deity, perform the seal of the Tathāgata’s empowerment."
Without altering the previous mudrā-form, one should recite this mantra.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the samaya-mudrās of the four Tathāgatas.
Each shall empower their body with their respective root mantras:
Akṣobhya at the heart, Ratnasaṃbhava on the forehead,
Amitāyus at the throat, and Amoghasiddhi on the crown.
The mantra is:
"Oṃ vajrasattva dhiṣṭhā svāhā | Oṃ vajraratna dhiṣṭhā svāhā | Oṃ vajradharma dhiṣṭhā svāhā | Oṃ vajrakarma dhiṣṭhā svāhā. Having thus empowered the body, one should next confer the empowerment.
The mudrās of the five Tathāgatas are each according to their samaya:
Samantaprabha sprinkles the crown of the head; Akṣobhya is at the forehead;
Ratnasambhava is on the right side of the crown; Amitāyus is at the back of the crown.
The Buddha Amoghasiddhi should be placed to the left of the crown.
The mantra is:

"Oṃ sarvatathāgatādhipataye viṣkira hūṃ oṃ vajrasattva viśodhaya hūṃ | oṃ vajraratna viśodhaya traḥ | oṃ vajrapadma viśodhaya hrīḥ | oṃ vajrakarma viśodhaya aḥ. Following the consecration, one should fasten the Tathāgata’s garland.
The Tathāgatas of the four directions all employ the samaya-mudrā:
with the two hands before the forehead, they form three knots behind the crown;
then, like a sash, they hang forward, first opening from the *vajra-pāṇi* (thumb and ring finger).

"Oṃ vajrasattvamāla viśodhaya vaṃ | Oṃ vajraratnamāla viśodhaya vaṃ | Oṃ vajrapadmamāla viśodhaya vaṃ | Oṃ vajrakarmamāla viśodhaya vaṃ. Next, one should arouse great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) toward all sentient beings.
Within the inexhaustible cycle of birth and death, they constantly don the armor of the great vow;
for the sake of purifying the Buddha-lands, subduing all devas and māras,
and attaining supreme perfect enlightenment, they don the armor of the Tathāgata.
With two vajra-fists, extend the forefingers and thumbs at the heart;
interlace the fingers around the heart, back, navel, and both knees;
then the navel, waist, heart, both shoulders, throat, neck, forehead, and crown of the head.
Each performs three circumambulations to the right; slowly extending forward, they hang downward.
First emanating from the *vara* and *prajñā* [mudrās], they are immediately able to protect all beings, such that even the celestial Māras cannot destroy them.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, one should join the vajra-fingers, pressing the palms together and striking three times;
by the power of this mudrā, those bound are released, and those released are bound.
Thereupon, one forms a firm armor; the assembly of sages all rejoice, and one attains a vajra-body like that of Vajrasattva.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the body of manifest wisdom: with both hands in the vajra-bind, place the dhyāna and jñāna fingers into the palms.
Visualize a moon disc before the body, and within it, contemplate the deity, clearly beholding the marks and signs of excellence.
Having completely entered the vajra, one should form the fundamental mudrā before the body according to the ritual rules, and contemplate the Great Sattva.
The mantra is:
"Vajrasattva Āḥ. Next, bind the seal of the body of vision and wisdom; the mudrā is as described previously.
Visualizing that Wisdom-Sattva, one should contemplate him within one's own body, summoning, entering, binding, and pleasing him to bring about accomplishment.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the four-syllable vidyā; the mudrā is like Trailokyavijaya.
First, extend [the hands] in the shape of a hook; next, extend the thumbs and interlace them.
Still, one should bend the heads so they touch, next the fingers should be interlocked,
and then the wrists joined and shaken.
By means of these four mudrās of illumination, one summons, attracts, binds, and gladdens.
The mantra says:
This samaya-mudrā should be formed by binding the vajra-fist, with the thumbs and ring fingers extended upright like needles; thus one accomplishes the yoga of the principal deity.
Recite the samaya:
"Samantaprasara-candaro enters from behind; within it, one should visualize the essence of the sattva:
'I am the samayasattva.'"
The mantra says:
Next, one should visualize a great ocean of water possessing the eight meritorious qualities;
above it, one visualizes a golden tortoise, surrounded by the seven golden mountains.
Visualize that within the mountain grove there is a river, entirely composed of water possessing the eight virtues;
visualize the seed syllables and recite *haṃ*, *vaṃ*, and *pra*.
The mantra is as follows:
"Oṃ vimarudati hūṃ. Next, visualize Mount Sumeru, composed entirely of the four precious jewels.
The mantra is:
"Visualize a jeweled pavilion above," and then form the vajra-wheel mudrā.
By the power of this mudrā, one then accomplishes all maṇḍalas.
With both hands in vajra-fists, the thumbs and ring fingers form hooks;
within these, one should visualize the maṇḍala according to the original teachings.
Then, within the jeweled pavilion, one should behold the maṇḍala.
Next, one should recite the invocation;
without altering the previous mudrā, one should visualize all the holy deities descending into this maṇḍala.
The invocation says:
Next, bind the seal for opening the gate; visualize the opening of the great mandala gate.
With both hands in the vajra-fist, hook the thumbs and wisdom fingers together.
Joining the *vajra* fists with the thumbs upright and pressed together, one should recite the mantra for each gate and then open them with the syllable HŪṂ.
Proceeding from the east and circling to the right, face toward each gate; if the space is too narrow, [adjust accordingly].
One should immediately perform visualization within the mind, operating the thought according to the original instructions.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the mudrā of invocation and address the Holy Honored One:
Form the *vajrabandha* with both hands; join the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhi* fingers upright;
bend the *vīrya* and *bala* fingers like hooks; leave the middle and ring fingers unjoined.
Invoke the name [of the deity] and request [his presence], reciting the *gāthā* three times:
Next, contemplate the ocean-like assembly of Buddhas, where all the sages have gathered like clouds;
they join their arms and snap their fingers, and the sound of those snaps pervades the entire Dharma-realm.
The mantra is as follows:
"Oṃ vajrasamāja jaḥ. All the Tathāgatas assembled in the sky, and having recited the one hundred and eight names, they paid homage to the assembly of the maṇḍala, praising it as follows:
Next, bind the mudrās of the four vidyās: The mudrā is like that of Trailokyavijaya;
hooking the *jñāna-pāda* (wisdom-step) to summon; the *pāśa-pāda* (lasso-step) is like a ring.
With the clasps opened and the wrists interlocked, and the bells joined at the wrists and shaken,
each recites their own mantra.
The mantra is as follows:
"Oṃ vajra-kuśa-jak vajra-pāśa hūṃ vajra-sphoṭa vaṃ vajra-veśa aḥ. Next, perform the vajra-clapping gesture to cause the assembly of noble ones to rejoice.
The mantra says:
Next, enter the wisdom of equality; holding the argha water, visualize bathing the bodies of all the holy ones, and you shall attain the stage of consecration.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the bell mudrā; with the right hand holding the vajra and the left shaking the bell, one enters the liberation of sound within the mind and contemplates the principle of prajñā.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the karma-mudrā and practice it at the heart;
clearly visualize the moon-disc of the heart, within which there is a karma-vajra.
One should form the vajra-fist, divide it into two with equal concentration;
the left fist, formed as a vajra-fist, grasps the tip of its own forefinger;
the left fist is placed at the navel, while the right forefinger hangs down, touching the ground.
The left fist is as described before; the right hand forms the *varada* (boon-granting) mudrā.

The two hands are crossed with palms facing upward; the *tarjanī* (forefinger) and *anāmikā* (ring finger) are held upright with their backs against each other, while the *madhyamā* (middle finger) and *kaniṣṭhikā* (pinky) are placed crosswise at their tips. The left fist is then placed again at the navel.
With the right hand extended in the gesture of fearlessness, these are the mudrās of the five Tathāgatas.
Their respective mantras are as follows:
Next, one should form the mudrās of the four Pāramitās, which are the karma-mudrās.
Each according to the seal of their respective original Buddha, they recite the mantras.
The mantras for each are as follows:
Next, one performs the ritual of the *karma-mudrā* for the sixteen honored ones.
The left fist rests at the side of the waist; the right hand, like a feathered arrow, grips and hurls the mallet.
The two fists cross and embrace the chest; advancing with strength, the hooking hand beckons.
The two fists follow the method of archery; at the heart, one snaps the fingers.
The advancing power has a jewel-like form; it revolves like a sun-disk within the heart.
Resting the right elbow upon the left fist, the two fists are opened upward toward the mouth.
This is the mudrā of the left lotus and the right opening; one visualizes holding a flower with the left hand.
The right hand is as if grasping a sword; with the fist inverted, advance the force and brace it.
Rotate halfway at the navel, then extend it together to the mouth and scatter it upward.
First, extend from the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* fingers; whirl and dance over the heart and both cheeks.
The Vajra-palms at the crown; the two fists don the armor;
the teeth of the effort, wisdom, dhyāna, and prajñā [fingers]—the two fists joined together.
These are the seals of the sixteen Great Beings and the eight inner and outer offerings.
And furthermore, regarding the four protections, I shall now explain their mudrās:
With both fists at the sides of the waist, slightly bowing the head to the left,
the two fists bind a garland that hangs down from behind the forehead and crown.
Join the two fists together sideways; from the navel to the mouth, they disperse.
The two fists perform the dance gesture, rotating the palms at the crown of the head.
According to the ritual of the Vajra-fist, one performs the four mudrās for burning incense and so forth.
Next, perform the seals of the three times: the hook, the chain, and so forth—the four means of attraction.
With fists clenched, scatter them downward;
then, scattering upward as if making an offering, extend the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* fingers vertically like needles, opening the palms to smear [the seal] across the chest.
The *jinya* (forefinger) is bent in the shape of a hook;
the *ryoku* (middle finger) is curved and the two fingers are interlaced at their tips. With the wrists joined, move them slightly.
The respective mantras are as follows:
With the right hand at the heart and the left pressing the ground, circumambulate the four sides of the wheel-maṇḍala,
reciting the mantra once for each side to establish the stations of the Bhadrakalpa.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the samaya: visualize a vajra upon the tongue;
first join the palms in the vajra gesture, then form the vajra-bond.
With the *tarjanī* and *anāmikā* fingers shaped like swords, place the *madhyamā* and *tarjanī* fingers along the back.
The *kṣānti* and *praṇidhāna* fingers are held upright like needles; the others are bent back like precious jewels.
The secret fingers are bent like lotus petals, their faces joined within the palms.
The *dāna*, *prajñā*, *dhyāna*, and *jñāna* fingers are joined together; these constitute the seals of the five Buddhas.
The respective mantras are as follows:
Next, bind the samaya mudrās and the four pāramitā mudrās,
each according to the seal of its respective primary Buddha, while reciting their individual mantras.
The respective mantras are:
VAJRAŚRĪ HŪṂ VAJRAGARBI TARĀ KRAMAṆI HOḤ. Next, one binds the sixteen deities: the eight offerings and the four means of attraction.
For the Samaya-mudrā: extend the *tarjanī* and *anāmikā* fingers upright like needles;
open and extend the little and ring fingers; next, perform the Vajra-bond;
bend the *tarjanī* and middle fingers like hooks; and because of those hooks, cross and extend them upward.
Without untying the bind, snap the fingers; extend the thumb and index finger fully, then bend them back without changing their positions.
Extend all six fingers and rotate them;
the first two remain unchanged as well. Bind the middle finger and lower four fingers like banners.
Without changing the previous mudrā-form, turn the hands open and spread them at the mouth;
join the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* fingers and extend them upright; bend the *vīrya* fingers like a lotus;
join the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhāna* fingers and extend them upright, bending the upper joints like a sword.
The patience and vow fingers enter the binding; the four upright and five upright fingers cross.
From the binding, the lotus of advancing power arises; the dhyāna and wisdom fingers open, leaning one upon the other.
The six pāramitās form a crossed seal and cover; the large fingers each grasp the small finger-nails.
Point the *vajra* at the heart; open with the *vajra*, *dāna*, and *prajñā*.
Form a small upright *vajra-hook*; bind the large and pinch the small root.
Support its back with the *vajra*; bind the reclining and upright *dhyāna* and *prajñā*.
This mudrā: bend [the thumbs] against the forehead; spread them upward from the navel;
rotate the palms at the crown of the head; release downward from the *yoga-pīṭha* bind;
offer by opening upward from the *yoga-pīṭha* bind; and join the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* fingers like needles from the *yoga-pīṭha* bind.
Unloose the binding at the chest; from the binding, advance like a hook.
Enter the wisdom-tiger’s mouth through dhyāna; the upper four cross like a ring.
As dhyāna and wisdom enter the palm and shake, the four seals become a single bond.
The respective mantras are as follows:
Next is the Great Offering Mudrā; to make offerings to all the Tathāgatas, one should form the Vajra-bond, with the seal-signs arising from the heart.
First, one binds the ritual mudrā of the Universal Illuminator (Samantaprabha):
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatavajradhātvaṣṭarabhūja spharaṇasamaye hūṃ. Next is the ritual mudrā of Vajrasattva.
“Oṃ sarvatathāgatavajrasattvādhiṣṭhānapūjāspharaṇasamaye hūṃ. This is the Vajraratnakarmamudrā.
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatavajraratnābhiṣekapūjāspharaṇasamaye hūṃ. Next is the Vajradharma-karma-mudrā.
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatavajradharmodgata-prabhāsvara-samaye hūṃ. Next is the Vajrakarma-karmamudrā.
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatavajrakarmānudrābhūṣaṇasamaye hūṃ. Next, the secret mantra for the vajra-bind at the heart is:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatasarvatmanirjātābhūṣaṇakarmavajri āḥ. The secret mantra for the right side is:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgata-sarvatman-nirjaya-tanapūja-spharaṇa-karma-kṣiro. The secret mantra for the left side is:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgata-sarvātman-nirjaya-tana-nurāgaṇa-pūja-spharaṇa-karma-vanidhruha. The secret mantra for the back of the waist is:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgata-sarvatma-nirjātana-sādhu-kāra-prayoga-spharaṇa-karmotsṛja-svaḥ. The secret mantra for the forehead is:
"Oṃ namas sarvatathāgata-viśvakara-taniprāva-jramaṇi oṃ. The mantra for the heart, which revolves like the form of a solar disc, is:
"Oṃ namas sarvatathāgatasūryavajrāditye vajrayi. With these secret words, extend the two arms upward for a long duration.
The secret words for releasing the smile upon the mouth are: "Oṃ namas sarvatathāgatābhipralambanajñānamaṇivajrajvālāvajratvaritaraṃ."
"Oṃ namas sarvatathāgatamahābhiṣekapramukhyakari-prabhavajrahasya haḥ. The mantra for the upper mouth is:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatavajradharmatāsamādhipraviṣṭo 'smi mahādharmakīrtaye. The mantra for the left ear is:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgataprajñāpāramitāvinirhāre sādhumati mahākūṣānujñe taṃ. The mantra for the right ear is:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatacakrākṣaraparivartana sarvasūtrāntanayāye sādhumati sarvamaṇḍale hūṃ. The mantra for the back of the head is:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgata-sandhāpasa-buddha-saṃgīty-abhyudgata-namastu namo vajravārīccha. The mantra for the crown of the head is:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatadhopamiga-samudra-spharaṇa-pūjākarma-karaka. The mantra for the right shoulder is:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgata-ṣpaprāsara-spharaṇa-pūjā-karomi kili kili jva. This is the mantra for the right hip.
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatā-lokajvala-spharaṇa-pūjā-karomi vara-pra. Next, place this mantra upon the heart.
Then, perform the gesture of scattering flowers and observe the ten directions.
"I now entreat all Buddhas to turn the wheel of Dharma.
One should further form this thought:
"In this Jambudvīpa and throughout the worlds of the ten directions, may the flowers born from the minds of humans and devas [be offered]."
All flowers found upon land and in water, I offer them all to the ten directions—
to all the great sattvas, the various retinues within their families,
and the deities of mudrās, mantras, and secret speech; I make this universal offering.
Because all Tathāgatas perform their enlightened activities,
the secret mantra says:
Furthermore, bind the mudrā of incense and contemplate as follows:
The fragrance of the essential nature of humans and devas, The fragrance of compounded and transformed substances—
Because of the Tathāgata’s *karma*, I now offer them all.
The secret mantra says:
Next, bind the mudrā of scented unguents: The fundamental essence-fragrance of humans and devas,
and compounded, transformed fragrances— such diverse fragrances,
through the Tathāgata’s karma, I now offer them all.
The secret instruction says:
Having next bound the mudrā of the lamp, one should contemplate thus:
"The fundamental nature of humans and devas arises, as well as their various radiant lights."
For the sake of performing activities, I now offer them all.
The secret mantra is:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgatānīpabhujyamāna-samudra-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ*. Regarding the Samaya-jewel mudrā, one should form this thought:
This realm and other realms, the various types of jewels on the mountain of treasures,
those within the earth and within the oceans—
all these I now offer, for the sake of the Tathāgata’s ritual activity (*karma*).
The secret instruction says:
Having formed the seal of playful sport, one should reflect thus:
"Whatever playthings exist among humans and devas," "all these various amusements," [are to be abandoned].
Jokes, music, and musical instruments— since all these are for the purpose of making offerings to the Buddha and performing his work, I now present them as an offering.
The secret mantra says:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgata-hāsya-locana-kṛtānugrahātiśayā-nuttara-pūjā-megha-samudra-samaye hūṃ. Having bound the *sattva-samādhi*, one should reflect as follows:
"These wish-granting trees (*kalpavṛkṣa*) and the like, which are able to provide various garments and requisites for adorning the body—all these are for the sake of making offerings."
Because one performs activities, I shall now offer this.
The secret mantra says:
*karmasamaya*. One should then reflect as follows:
Within the treasury of space, all the Tathāgatas reside;
for the sake of serving them, I imagine myself before each and every Buddha,
attending and serving them with devotion.
The secret mantra says:
"Dharma-samaya. Then one should reflect thus:
"I am now this very body, equal to all the bodhisattvas."
Contemplating that the true nature of phenomena is attained as equal and without distinction—
having performed this contemplation, one recites this secret mantra. The mantra is:
By the samaya of the Jewel Banner, one should contemplate all classes of sentient beings within the midst of birth and death, who are entangled by suffering and affliction;
because of the arising of deep compassion, I now act for their rescue and protection.
And protect the bodhicitta; cause those not yet crossed over to cross over, and those not yet settled to find peace;
cause all to attain nirvana, and rain down various treasures, so that all their aspirations may be fulfilled.
Having reflected thus, one recites this secret mantra.
The secret mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the mudrā of the fragrant body, the samaya-unguent.
And he reflects thus:
"May all unwholesome deeds of the three karmas be entirely abandoned;
may all wholesome dharmas be fully accomplished."
The secret mantra is:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānamahāmogha-kāśilaparāmitābhūjamīyāsamunnataspharaṇasamaye hūṃ*. Having performed the *karma-mudrā* by touching the ground, one should further form this thought:
"May all sentient beings possess minds of loving-kindness and be free from affliction and harm."
Far removed from all fears, they gaze upon one another with joyful hearts;
adorned with all the marks and signs of excellence, they have realized the profound treasury of Dharma.
The secret mantra says:
Victorious in the battle through diligence, clad in the armor of the samaya, they reflect thus:
"May all sentient beings who practice the bodhisattva path don this firm armor."
The secret instruction says:
Forming the samādhi mudrā, one should contemplate as follows regarding the Buddha of the North, Karma:
Having subdued the afflictions and the enemies that are the secondary afflictions,
and having attained profound meditative concentration, one recites this mantra.
The mantra says:
Having bound the seal of the World-Illuminating Bhagavān and the supreme *karma*-mudrā,
he reflects thus:
"I shall accomplish the five vidyās, both mundane and supramundane."
Wisdom is universally perfected, and one attains the vision of reality;
removing the cognitive hindrances of affliction, with eloquence, fearlessness, and so forth,
the Buddha-dharma adorns the mind.
Then recite this mantra.
The secret words say:
"The supreme samādhi; next, one should form the mudrā."
Interlace the two outer hands, join the thumbs and index fingers together, and place them facing upward within the chest; one should then contemplate thus:
"I realize the true nature of phenomena—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness."
All phenomena are exactly like this.
Having contemplated them thus, one recites the secret mantra.
The secret words are as follows:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatādhyeṣaṇamahāpratiṣṭhāpūjāmoghasamudrā-samaye hūṃ. Next, one should join the fingertips and form this thought:
"As I now utter these words, may all sentient beings hear them in their entirety."
And recite this secret mantra.
The secret words say:
Having thus extensively performed the Buddha-activities, one should next perform the recitation with a concentrated mind.
Surrounded by one’s own assembly of followers, abiding in the Great Mirror-like Wisdom of Parinirvāṇa,
one should form the Vajrasamaya mudrā and recite the hundred-syllable Vajra mantra three,
five, or seven times; thereafter, recite the Vajrasattva mantra the same number of times.
Recite the hundred-syllable mantra as follows:
Next, one should hold the rosary and recite the mantra seven times;
then, using the empowerment phrases, empower it according to the ritual rules.
Sitting upright according to the ritual rules,
one should recite with vajra-speech either one thousand or one hundred times, as desired.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the Lotus Samaya mudrā; having recited the root mantra seven times, one should then recite the hundred-syllable mantra of the Lotus, either once, thrice, or up to seven times.

This *Lotus Hundred-Syllable Mantra* is the same as the aforementioned *Vajra Hundred-Syllable Mantra*, with the sole exception that "padya" and the subsequent seed-syllable are changed to "jri" (a conjunct). This refers to the two hands holding a rosary; recite the root mantra seven times while holding the rosary to the crown of the head and the heart, thereby consecrating it with the mantra.
The mantra is as follows:
Having consecrated the jewel, one should recite it while abiding in meditative equipoise;
without moving the tip of the tongue excessively, with both lips and teeth closed.
Accomplishing the teaching of the secret speech, the vajra speech is free from sound;
following the body to contemplate the marks and signs, one must not let this lapse at any of the four times.
A hundred thousand is the limit, yet one should further exceed this.
With supernormal powers, merit, and wisdom, manifesting in this world as a sattva;
when the recitation reaches its limit, hold the rosary and make the great vow,
bind the samādhi mudrā, and enter the dharma-dhātu samādhi.
The practitioner emerges from samādhi, immediately binds the root mudrā,
and recites the root mantra seven times; then, performing the eight offerings and praising with sublime sounds, they present the argha perfumed water.
Next, seal the three times with the left-turning gesture to dissolve the boundary;
then, form the samaya-fist and pull it open while reciting once;
next, form the karma-fist and open the hands three times while reciting three times.
From each and every [source], all mudrās arise;
they should be understood in their respective places by means of this heart-mantra.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, form the mudrā for the respectful dismissal:
with both hands in the vajra-bind, join the *tarjanī* and *anāmikā* fingers like lotus petals, and place the tips of the fingers upon the seasonal flowers.
Having recited the mantra, cast them upward to respectfully dismiss the assembly of noble ones.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, one should form the Jewel Seal (*ratnamudrā*):
with both hands in the Vajra-bond, the thumbs and index fingers are shaped like jewels; the ring and little fingers are likewise so formed.
The mudrā arises from the heart and is placed at the site of consecration;
with hands joined like a binding garland, one next forms the armor mudrā.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, having donned the armor, one should clap the joined palms three times to gladden the assembly of noble ones; by means of this heart-mantra,
one is released from bonds and attains joy, obtaining a vajra-body.
The mantra says:
Having escorted the Honored Sage away, one should form the empowerment mudrā,
recite the vidyā while applying it to the four places, and perform the consecration and donning of the armor.

Furthermore, perform the ritual of the mudrās; as with the mudrās of the four Buddhas previously mentioned, perform the confession and the making of vows, and thereafter dwell in a quiet and secluded place.
Adorn the site with incense and flowers, and abide in samādhi.
Recite and chant the Mahāyāna scriptures, Walking meditation as you please.
